marks.gloss_en: תניא נמי הכי, רבי נתן אומר: מנין שאין הקדוש ברוך הוא מואס בתפלתן של רבים -- שנאמר הן אל כביר ולא ימאס, וכתיב פדה בשלום נפשי: the baraita derives from R' Acha's two verses
the Holy One does not despise the prayer of the many
דאמר רבי יהושע בן לוי לבניה: קדימו וחשיכו ועיילו לבי כנישתא כי היכי דתורכו חיי -- as R' Yehoshua ben Levi told his sons that the practice lengthens life
R' Yehoshua ben Levi to his sons: go early and stay late and enter the synagogue, so that you may live long
תמה ואמר: למען ירבו ימיכם וימי בניכם על האדמה כתיב, אבל בחוצה לארץ לא? -- length of days is promised upon the Land; how then are there old men in Babylonia?
כיון דאמרי ליה מקדמי ומחשכי לבי כנישתא, אמר: היינו דאהני להו -- once told that they go early and stay late at the synagogue: that is what availed them (= p_hainu_deahani_lehu)
there are old men in Babylonia
שני פתחים סלקא דעתך?! -- two doorways, literally: can that be what is meant?
אלא אימא: שיעור שני פתחים, ואחר כך יתפלל -- rather say: the measure of two doorways, and then pray (= p_shiur_shnei_petachim)
Rav Chisda: a person should always enter two doorways into the synagogue
'but as for me, my prayer is to You, Lord, at a time of favour' (Ps 69:14): when is a time of favour? at the hour when the congregation prays
R' Yosei b. R' Chanina: from here -- 'thus says the Lord: at a time of favour I have answered you' (Isa 49:8)
R' Acha b. R' Chanina: from here -- 'behold, God is mighty and despises not' (Job 36:5)
whoever has a synagogue in his town and does not enter it to pray is called an evil neighbour
תניא נמי הכי: 903 kinds of death were created, שנאמר למות תוצאות -- the baraita reads the same verse of death
the baraita: nine hundred and three kinds of death were created in the world -- from 'issues of death', totzaot being 903 in gematria
מאי קרא -- ישישו כי ימצאו קבר: 'finding' is said of a grave
היינו דאמרי אינשי -- the saying that one should pray for mercy until the last shovelful is this reading in popular form
R' Yochanan: 'the time of finding' is burial
והיינו דאמר רבי חייא בר אמי משמיה דעולא -- God's only place in the world is the four cubits of halakha, which is why He loves the halakha-gates over synagogues and study halls
Ulla: since the day the Temple was destroyed, the Holy One has in His world only the four cubits of halakha
R' Chanina: 'the time of finding' (Ps 32:6) is a wife
in the West, when a man married they would ask him: matza or motze? -- matza as in 'he who finds a wife finds good' (Prov 18:22), motze as in 'and I find the woman more bitter than death' (Eccl 7:26)
R' Natan: 'the time of finding' is Torah
Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak: 'the time of finding' is death
Mar Zutra: 'the time of finding' is a privy
Rav Chisda: 'the Lord loves the gates of Zion more than all the dwellings of Jacob' (Ps 87:2) -- the Lord loves gates distinguished in halakha more than synagogues and study halls
Abaye: at first I studied at home and prayed in the synagogue
R' Ami and R' Asi, though they had thirteen synagogues in Tiberias, prayed only between the pillars where they studied
R' Ami: 'they who forsake the Lord shall perish' (Isa 1:28) -- this is one who leaves the Torah scroll [while it is out] and goes out
R' Abbahu would go out between one reader and the next
Rav Sheshet would turn his face away [from the reading] and study
Ulla: greater is one who benefits from his own labour than a God-fearer
R' Ami: a person should always complete his portions with the congregation -- twice Scripture and once Targum
והתניא: אל ידור -- but a baraita teaches that one should NOT live in his teacher's place
the baraita: one should not live [in his teacher's place]
לא קשיא: הא דכייף ליה, הא דלא כייף ליה -- Ulla speaks of one who submits to his teacher, the baraita of one who does not (= p_yadur_dekayif_leih, p_al_yadur_delo_kayif_leih)
Ulla's 'let him live there' speaks of one who submits to his teacher
Ulla: one should always live in the place where his teacher lives
